translations.text: The words of Nehemiah son of Hacaliah. In the month of Kislev, in the twentieth year of King Artaxerxes, I was in Susa, the capital of Abira.
One of my brothers came to me, along with men of Judah, and I asked them about those who had survived and come out of captivity, and about Jerusalem.

They said to me, “Those who escaped captivity are there in their own land, in great distress and disgrace. The walls of Jerusalem remain broken down and ruined, and its gates have been burned with fire.”
When I heard these words, I sat down and wept. I mourned for days, fasted, and prayed before the Lord, the God of heaven.
I said, “Lord, God of heaven and earth, you are mighty, great, and awesome. You keep your covenant and show mercy to those who love you and obey your laws.

Let your ears hear and your eyes see. Now hear and see the prayer of your servant, which I offer before you today for the children of Israel, your servants. We were handed over to distress because of the sins we committed. Both I and my father’s household have sinned.
For we have transgressed greatly and have not kept your laws, commands, and judgments, which you commanded us through your servant Moses.
Remember, Lord, your word, which you commanded your servant Moses, saying, ‘If you do not keep my laws, I will scatter you among the nations.

But if you return and keep my laws and carry them out, even if you are scattered to the ends of the earth, I will gather you from there and bring you to the place I will choose, where my name dwells.’
Now these are your servants and your people, whom you redeemed by your great power and your uplifted arm.

Do not withdraw your hand, but let your ears attend to the prayers of your servants and listen to the requests of those who fear your name. Grant success to your servant’s request today, and let me find compassion before this man.” I was the king’s cupbearer.
In the month of Nisan, in the twentieth year of King Artaxerxes, he asked me for wine. I took the wine and gave it to the king, and the king was alone.
When he drank the wine, he said to me, “Why is your face sorrowful and sad? There is no reason for this except trouble in your heart.” I was very afraid.
I said to the king, “May you live forever, O king! Why should my face not be sorrowful and sad? The city and my father’s house are deserted, and the gates have been destroyed by fire.”
The king said to me, “For what purpose are you making this request?” I prayed and lifted my thoughts to the Lord, the God of heaven.

I said to the king, “May there be goodness upon your kingdom. If your servant has found favor before you, and you are willing, send me to Judea, to the city of my ancestors’ memorials, and I will rebuild it at your command.”
The king, and his concubine who sat beside him, said to me, “When will you arrive, and when will you return?” The king showed me kindness and let me go, and I set a time with him.
I said to the king, “If I have found favor before you, give me letters to the governors of the regions along the River, so that they may escort me until I reach Judea,

and a letter to Asaph, the keeper of the royal park, so that he may give me timber for constructing the gates and walls of the city, and the house I will enter there.” The king granted this to me because the hand of my God was upon me for good.
I came to the governors of the River and gave them the king’s letters. The king had sent military commanders and horses with me.
Sanballat the governor and Tobiah the Ammonite servant heard, and it displeased them because I sought men for the welfare and needs of Israel.
I came to Jerusalem and stayed there for three days.
I rose during the night, with a few men accompanying me. I did not tell the men what God had put into my heart to do for Israel. There was no animal with me except the animal on which I was riding.

I went out through the Torrent Gate, past the opening of the fig-tree land, and as far as the Gate of the Springs. I was squeezed by the narrowness of the passage beside the wall of Jerusalem, which they had cleared away, and its gates had been destroyed by fire.
I passed through the Gate of the Spring, beside the king’s fountains, but there was no room there for my animal to pass with me riding on it.
During the night I went up to the wall beside the torrent. I was squeezed by the narrow passage along the wall, and I reached the Valley Gate.
I returned, and the guards did not know where I had gone or what I was doing. Until then, the Jews, the priests, the nobles, the commanders, and the others carrying out the work had not been told.
I said to them, “You see the trouble we are now in, and how Jerusalem is deserted and its gates are burned. Come, let us build the walls of Jerusalem, so that we will no longer be a disgrace.”

I told them about the hand of the Lord, which was with me for good, and about the words the king had spoken to me. I said to them, “Now come, let us rise and build.” And their hands were strengthened for good.
And Sanballat, Tobiah the Ammonite servant, and Geshem the Arab heard about it and mocked us. They came to us and said, “What is this that you are doing? Do you intend to rebel against the king?”
I answered them, saying, “The God of heaven and earth has given us success. We are his holy servants, and we are building this city. But you have no share, memorial, or right in Jerusalem.”
Eliashib the high priest and his fellow priests rose and built the gate of the aqueduct’s pools. They consecrated it and set up its doors, and they built it up as far as the Tower of Hananel.
By the hands of the sons of the men of Jericho, and by the hands of the sons of Zaccur, the sons of Imri.
The sons of Hassenaah built the [?] Gate. They put it in order and fitted it with its locks and bars.
Next to them, Meshullam son of Berechiah, son of Meshezabel, worked; and next to them, Zadok son of Baana worked.
And beside them the men of Tekoa [?] worked, and they did not put their necks into their service.
Judah, the sons of Paseah, and Meshullam son of Besodeiah worked on the Old Gate. They fitted it out and set up its doors, locks, and bars.
After them, next in line, Hananiah son of Rokeim worked, and he left it to the people of Jerusalem as far as the wall of the public squares.
After them, Rephaiah, governor of the districts of Jerusalem, worked.
Next to him, Jedaiah son of Harumaph worked beside his own house; and next to him, Hattush son of Hashabneiah worked.
Hilkiah son of Harim and Hasshub son of Pahath-moab worked on the second section, as far as the Tower of the Ovens.
Next to him, Shallum son of Hallohesh, governor of half the district of Jerusalem, worked, together with his daughters.
Hanun and those who lived in Zanoah worked on the Valley Gate. They built it and set up its doors, locks, and bars, and they built a thousand cubits of the wall as far as the Ash Gate.
Malchijah son of Rechab, governor of the district of Beth-haccherem, worked on the Ash Gate, together with his towns. They roofed it and set up its doors, locks, and bars.
Adion, the king’s governor, worked on the wall of the flowing spring as far as the steps that descend from the City of David.
After him, Nehemiah son of Azbuk, governor of the district of Beth-zur, worked as far as the garden of David’s grounds, as far as the constructed fountains, and as far as Beth-haggibborim.
Next to him the Levites made repairs: Rehum son of Bani; and beside them Hashabiah, ruler of the district of Keilah, made repairs.
Next to him his brothers made repairs: Binnui son of Hadad, ruler of the district of Keilah.
Next to him Ezer son of Jeshua, ruler of Mizpah, repaired a second section of the wall, which went up and joined the corners of the tower.
After him Baruch son of Zabbai repaired a second section, from the corner to the door of the house of Eliashib, where the high priest was.
Next to him Meremoth son of Uriah, son of Hakkoz, repaired a second section, from the doors of the house of Eliashib to its end.
Next to him the priests, men of Aker, made repairs. Next to him Benjamin and Hasshub made repairs in front of their houses.
Next to him Azariah son of Maaseiah, son of Ananiah, made repairs near his house.
Next to him Binnui son of Henadad repaired a second section, from the house of Azariah to the corner and the place where the wall turned.
Palal son of Uzai repaired the section opposite the corner and the tower outside the king’s palace, above the prison courtyard. After him came Pedaiah son of Parosh.
And the temple servants who lived in Ophel, at the garden of the Water Gate on the east side and the tower on the outer side.
Next to him the people of Tekoa repaired a second section, opposite the great projecting tower, as far as the wall of Ophel.
Above the Horse Gate the priests made repairs, each man opposite his own house.
Next to him Zadok son of Immer made repairs opposite his house. Next to him Shemaiah son of Shecaniah, who was the keeper of the East Gate, made repairs.
Next to him Hananiah son of Shelemiah and Hanun son of Zalaph repaired a second section. Next to him Meshullam son of Berechiah made repairs opposite the treasury of his house.
Next to him Malchijah son of Zareph made repairs as far as Bethanathan, and other wealthy men of the city made repairs opposite the Gate of Miphkad, as far as the ascent of the surrounding structure.
Between the gates of the springs, Hilkiah and the wealthy men of the city made repairs.
When Sanballat heard that we were building the wall and erecting its towers, he was displeased and became very angry, and he mocked Judea.
He said before his brothers, “Is this your strength, Samaritans? And how are the Jews building and fortifying their cities?”

Tobiah the Ammonite came to see them and said, “They will not be able to build and offer sacrifices, or eat the offerings in their own place. Will not foxes now come up and tear down the stones of its walls?” And we say:
“Hear us, Lord our God, for we have become objects of contempt and disgrace. Turn their insults back upon their own heads, and give them over to disgrace before their captors,
and do not let their lawless deeds be covered.”

And when Sanballat and Tobiah, the Arabs and the Ammonites, heard that the rebuilding of Jerusalem’s wall was succeeding and that we had begun to make the work visible in each place, they were displeased.
And they all gathered together to come and fight against Jerusalem.
We prayed to the Lord our God and stationed guards over ourselves day and night because of our enemies.
The men of Judea said, “We cannot fight like this and build at the same time. Instead, let some stand ready with weapons, and let others build.”
Those who were harassing us said, “We will not let them know or see until we rise from our respective places, come among them, kill them, and stop their work.”
When the Jews who lived in various places came, they said to us, “They will come out suddenly against us from every place.”
I stationed men in the lowest places behind the wall, under the roofs, with their weapons, spears, and bows.

And I rose and said to the men who stood equipped and ready, to their commanders, and to those who were guards at the various posts: “Do not be afraid of them. Remember our great and awesome God, and fight for your brothers, your wives, your sons, your daughters, and your homes.”
And when our enemies heard that we had learned of their plans and had equipped ourselves and made ready, God scattered their plans, and we all returned to building the wall, each man to his own work.

And from that day onward, half were assigned to the work, and half were armed against the enemies, with spears, shields, and bows in their hands. Each man stood ready behind his brother who was building the wall.
And at times he helped his brother, holding his weapon in one hand and handing his brother rubble or mortar with the other.
And each of the builders had his sword at his waist and a single-edged blade on his [?], and in this way they built the wall of Jerusalem. The man who sounded the horn trumpet stood near them.

And I said to those who stood armed and ready and to their leaders: “The work is great and extensive, and we are scattered along the wall under construction, far from one another, each man from his brother.
So let us station men who sound the trumpets at various places. Whenever anyone hears the sound of the horn trumpet, let everyone gather there, and our God will fight against our enemies for us.”
And half were working, while half held their weapons ready, from the break of dawn until the stars came out.
And I said to the men of the people: “Let us come and stay within the city of Jerusalem. At night let us set a guard around ourselves, and by day let us work.”
And I remained there with the men around me who guarded me, and none of us undressed or took off his weapons.
And a great outcry arose from the people and their wives, each against his brother.
And they said: “For the sake of our sons and daughters, whose food has run out, let us go and buy food so that we may live.”
And some said: “Let us pledge our fields and vineyards as security, obtain wheat, and eat.”
And there were some who said: “We gave up our possessions and obtained gold and silver, and paid them as taxes to the king.”

And now our bodies are like the bodies of our brothers, and our children are like their children. Why, then, have we given our sons into slavery? Our daughters have been taken by force, and we have no means in our hands by which to redeem them.
And I was deeply distressed when I heard their outcry and their words.
And I considered the matter in my mind and argued with their nobles and leaders. I said to them: “You are the ones demanding taxes from your brothers.” And I ordered them to hold a great assembly.
And I said to them: “We redeemed our Jewish brothers who had been sold to Gentiles whom we did not know, yet you sell them!” And they fell silent and could give no answer.
And I said: “What you are doing is not good, because you do not fear God, and because of this we have still not escaped the reproach of the Gentiles, our enemies.”
And I said to my brothers and acquaintances: “Let both you and me give silver and produce as ransom, which these tax collectors demand.
And let us return their fields, vineyards, olive groves, and houses today. With our silver, let them buy wheat, wine, and oil and bring them to these people.”

And the leaders and the other prominent men said: “We will give them back and demand nothing from these people. We will do as you have commanded.” And I called the priests and made them swear an oath concerning this matter.

And I shook out my cloak vigorously and said, “May God likewise shake every man who does not fulfill these words out of his livelihood and his dwelling places. May he thus be emptied and shaken out of his livelihood.” And all the people of that assembly said, “Amen.” They praised the Lord, and all the people acted upon and fulfilled these words.

And from the day when I commanded that they should have no governors of Judah, from the twentieth year until the thirty-second year of King Artaxerxes, for twelve years, my brothers and I were governors. We ate and drank nothing taken by force from anyone.

And I imposed a burden on those who had formerly exercised tyranny, and took from them bread and wine and all the other silver, forty didrachms, and returned it to its owners. I removed them from authority over the people, and I did not act like them, because of the fear of God.
And the work on the wall prospered, and I did not forcibly take anyone’s fields or vineyards. Everyone worked on the wall without interruption.
And I provided for a hundred men from among the Jews, and others who came to us from the nations around us, and included them at my table.

And each day there were one bull calf, six choice sheep, and one [?]. This was my daily expenditure. And every ten days I freely gave wine for everyone to drink. I took no bread from anyone by force, because I knew that the people’s work was burdensome.
May God remember me for good, in accordance with what I have done for all the people.

And it happened that Sanballat, Tobiah, the land of the Arabs, and many others among our enemies heard that I had built the wall and that no strength remained in them. Up to that time, however, the doors had not yet been fitted.
And Sanballat and Geshem sent to me, saying, “Come, let us meet together in a village on the plain of Ono.” But they intended to plot harm against me.
And I sent messengers to them and said, “The work I am doing is a great work, and I cannot come down to you, lest the work be interrupted. When I finish it, then I will come down to you.”
And they sent to me many times, and I gave them the same answer.
And Sanballat sent his servant to me, holding an open letter in his hand.

In it was written as follows: “A report has spread among all the nations that you and all the Jews intend to rebel against the king. That is why you are building your wall and strengthening its towers, because you intend to become king.

And for this reason you have appointed prophets for yourself, because you intend to take your seat in Jerusalem and reign over Judea. Now these words may be reported to the king. Come, and let the two of us discuss this.”
And I sent to him and said, “These words you speak have no basis anywhere. Rather, you are saying this out of your own heart.”
For they were all trying to frighten us, saying, “Let their hands grow weak, and let them not finish their work.” But now I strengthened my hands until the work was brought to completion.

And I entered the house of Shemaiah son of Delaiah, son of Mehetabel. He was keeping quiet in his house, and he said to me, “Let us gather in the house of the Lord and secure ourselves inside it, and let us shut its doors, lest the enemies come by night and kill us.”
And I said, “Who is that man from whom I should flee? And who is there, a man like me, who could enter the house of the Lord and survive?”
And I knew that he had not been sent by God, and that there was no prophetic word concerning me.
And Tobiah and Sanballat recruited hired men and many groups against me, so that I would be afraid and enter the house of the Lord and sin, and they would give me a bad name.
May God remember the treachery of Tobiah and Sanballat, who plotted evil against me and urged false prophecy to terrify and frighten me.
And the wall was completed on the twenty-fifth day of the month of Elul, in fifty-two days.
And when all our enemies heard, all the nations around us were terrified. Great dread and fear fell upon them, and they knew that our work had been completed through God.
In those days letters were sent with great honor from the Jews to Tobiah, and letters from Tobiah came to them.
For there were close family ties between them: he was the son-in-law of Shecaniah son of Arah, and his son Jehohanan had married the daughter of Meshullam son of Berechiah.
They brought his words to me and reported my words to him, and he sent many letters to frighten me.
When the wall was completed and I had set up its gates, the gatekeepers, singers, psalm singers, and Levites took their places.
And I gave instructions to my brothers and to Hananiah, who was ruler over Jerusalem, because he was a trustworthy man and feared God more than many others.

I said to them, “Do not open the gates early, before sunrise. While everyone is still awake, close the gates and secure them with bolts. Let guards from among the inhabitants of Jerusalem stand at the gates, each man at his assigned watch and each at his own house.”
For the city is large and spacious, but there are few people in it, and not all the houses have yet been built.

God put it into my heart, and I gathered the nobles, the rulers, and the people into one assembly. I found the genealogical register of those who had first come up from captivity, and this was written in it:

These are the names of the children of Israel who came up from captivity, whom Nebuchadnezzar, king of the Babylonians, had taken into exile. They returned to Jerusalem and Judea, each to his own city.
They came with Zerubbabel, Jeshua, Nehemiah, Azariah, Raamiah, Nahamani, Mordecai, Belman, Matatparath, Ezra, Bigvai, Nahum, Baanah, and Mophra. The men of the people of Israel:
The sons of Parosh: two thousand one hundred seventy-two.
The sons of Shephatiah: three hundred seventy-two.
The sons of Arah: six hundred fifty-six.
The sons of Pahath-moab, from the sons of Jeshua and Joab: two thousand two hundred eighteen.
The descendants of Elam: one thousand two hundred fifty-four.
The sons of Zattu: eight hundred forty-five.
The sons of Zaccai: seven hundred sixty.
The sons of Binnui: six hundred forty-eight.
The descendants of Bebai: six hundred forty-eight.
The sons of Aziah: two thousand three hundred twenty-two.
The sons of Adonikam: six hundred fifty-seven.
The sons of Bigvai: two thousand sixty-seven.
The sons of Adin: six hundred fifty-four.
The sons of Ater-Hezekiah: ninety-eight.
The sons of Bezai: three hundred twenty-four.
The sons of Hariph: one hundred twelve.
The sons of Gibeon: ninety-five.
The sons of Bethlehem: one hundred and twenty-three. The sons of Netophah: fifty-six.
The sons of Anathoth: one hundred and twenty-eight.
The sons of Beth-azmaveth: forty-two.
The sons of Kiriath-jearim, Chephirah, and Beeroth: eight hundred and forty-three.
The sons of Ramah and Geba: six hundred and twenty-one.
The sons of Michmas: one hundred and twenty-two.
The sons of Bethel and Ai: one hundred and twenty-three.
The sons of Nebo: one hundred and fifty-two. The sons of Magbish: one hundred and fifty-six.
The sons of Elam: one thousand and fifty-four.
The sons of Harim: three hundred and twenty.
The sons of Jericho: three hundred and forty-five.
The sons of Lod, Hadid, and Ono: seven hundred and twenty-three.
The sons of Ananah: three thousand one hundred and thirty.
The priests: the sons of Jedaiah, of the house of Jeshua: nine hundred and seventy-three.
The sons of Immer: one thousand and fifty-two.
The sons of Pashhur: one thousand two hundred and forty-seven.
The sons of Harim: one thousand and seventeen.
And the Levites: the descendants of Jeshua, Kadmiel, from among the descendants.
Hodaviah: seventy-four.
And the singers, the psalm singers, the sons of Asaph: one hundred and forty-eight.
And the gatekeepers: the sons of Shallum, the sons of Ater, the sons of Talmon, the sons of Akkub, the sons of Hatita, the sons of Shobai: one hundred and thirty-eight.
And the Nethinim: the sons of Ziha, the sons of Hasupha, the sons of Tabbaoth, the sons of Sarias, the sons of Sia, the sons of Padon.
The sons of Lebanah, the sons of Hagabah, the sons of Akkub, the sons of Uta, the sons of Ketar, the sons of Hagab, the sons of Shalmai.
The sons of Hanan, the sons of Giddel, the sons of Gahar.
The sons of Reaiah, the sons of Rezin, the sons of Nekoda.
The descendants of Gazzam, the descendants of Uzza, the descendants of Paseah.
The descendants of Besai, the descendants of Meunim, the descendants of Nephushesim.
The descendants of Bakbuk, the descendants of Hakupha, the descendants of Harhur.
The descendants of Bazluth, the descendants of Mehida, the descendants of Harsha.
The descendants of Barkos, the descendants of Sisera, the descendants of Temah.
The descendants of Neziah, the descendants of Hatipha.
The descendants of Solomon’s servants: the descendants of Sotai, the descendants of Sophereth, the descendants of Perida.
The descendants of Jaala, the descendants of Darkon, the descendants of Giddel.
The descendants of Shephatiah, the descendants of Etem, the descendants of Pochereth-hazzebaim, the descendants of Hemim.
All the temple servants and the descendants of Solomon’s servants: three hundred ninety-two.
These were the people who came up from Tel-melah, Tel-harsha, Cherub, Addon, and Immer, but could not establish their ancestral households or their lineage to show that they were from Israel.
The descendants of Delaiah, the descendants of Bua, the descendants of Tobiah, and the descendants of Nekoda: six hundred forty-two.

And from the priests: the descendants of Hobaiah, the descendants of Hakkoz, and the descendants of Barzillai, who had married one of the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite and was called by his name.
These sought the record of their genealogy, but it was not found, and they were excluded from the priesthood.
The governor said to them, “They must not eat any of the most holy things until a priest arises and, being enlightened, makes them known.”
The whole assembled congregation numbered forty-two thousand three hundred sixty.
This excluded their male and female servants, who numbered seven thousand three hundred thirty-seven, and the male and female singers who sang psalms, who numbered two hundred forty-five.
There were seven hundred thirty-six horses and two hundred forty-five mules.
There were four hundred thirty-five camels and six thousand twenty-seven donkeys.
The leaders, according to their ancestral households, contributed to the work. The governor gave to the treasury fifty gold bowls and thirty priestly robes.
The heads of the ancestral households gave to the treasury for the work twenty thousand in gold and ten thousand in silver, two thousand two hundred minas.
The rest of the people gave twenty thousand darics, two thousand silver vessels, and sixty-seven priestly robes.

And the priests, the Levites, the gatekeepers, the singers who sang psalms, some of the people, the temple servants, and all Israel settled in their towns. And the seventh month arrived, and the Israelites were in their towns.
All the people gathered as one man in the square before the Water Gate. They told Ezra, the scribe of the Lord’s law, to bring the law of Moses, which the Lord, the God of Israel, had commanded.
Ezra the priest brought the law before the congregation, where men, women, and everyone willing to listen had gathered, on the first day of the seventh month.

He began reading it in the morning, when the sun rose, and continued until noon, before the men and women. Everyone understood, and all the people listened attentively to everything written in the law.

Ezra the priest and scribe stood on a wooden platform. Beside him stood Mattithiah, Shemaiah, Ananiah, Uriah, Hilkiah, and Maaseiah on his right, and Pedaiah, Mishael, Malchijah, Hashum, Sardana, Zechariah, and Meshullam on his left.
When Ezra opened the book before all the people—for he was over all the people—as he opened the book, the people stood before him.
Ezra blessed the Lord, the great God, and all the people said, “Amen.” They raised their hands, bowed down, and worshiped the Lord God with their faces to the ground.
Jeshua, Bani, and Sherebiah explained the law to the people, and the people stood in their appointed places.

Nehemiah, who was the governor, Ezra the priest and scribe, and the Levites who explained things to the people said to all the people, “This day is holy to the Lord our God. Do not mourn or weep.” For the people were weeping when they heard the words of the law.
They said to them, “Go, eat rich foods and drink sweet drinks, and send portions to those who have nothing, because this day is holy to the Lord our God. Now take courage, and do not grieve him.”
The Levites quieted the people, saying, “Be quiet and do not be sad, because this day is holy.”
The people went to eat and drink, sent portions to those who had nothing, and celebrated with great joy, because they understood the words of the law that he had read to them.

On the second day, the heads of the ancestral families of all the people, the priests, and the Levites gathered around Ezra, the scribe of the law, to gain understanding and learn from him all the words of the law.
They found written in the law that the Lord God had commanded Moses that the Israelites should live in booths during the festival of the seventh month,

and that they should announce it by trumpet in all their cities and in Jerusalem. Ezra said, “Go out to the mountain and bring olive leaves, leaves from plane trees, leaves of fragrant myrtles, palm leaves, and leaves from densely branched trees, and make yourselves booths, as it is written.”

The people went out and brought them and made themselves booths, each man on his own roof and each man in his own courtyard, and in the courtyard of the house of God and in the city squares as far as the Gate of Ephraim.

The whole assembled congregation of those who had returned from captivity made booths and lived in them. For from the days of Joshua son of Nun until that day, the Israelites had never done so. And there was exceedingly great joy.

He read the book of the law day by day, from the first day through the seventh day. They celebrated the festival for seven days, and on the eighth day there was a concluding observance according to the law.
On the twenty-fourth day of the month, the Israelites gathered and began to fast. They put on sackcloth and sprinkled ashes on their heads.
The Israelites separated themselves from all foreigners and made atonement for their sins and the sins of their ancestors.
They stood in their places, and Ezra read the book of the law of the Lord God. All the people bowed down to the Lord their God.

Ezra and the Levites stood on a raised platform, along with Jeshua son of Jozadak, the sons of Kadmiel, Shecaniah son of Sherebiah, and the sons of Ananiah. They cried out loudly to the Lord their God.

The Levites Jeshua and Kadmiel said, “Brothers, bless the Lord our God forever and ever. May the glory of the Lord be blessed, and may blessing and thanksgiving to him be exalted.” Then Ezra began to bless the Lord God and said:

“You alone are the Lord God himself. You made the heavens and the heaven of heavens and all their hosts, the earth and all its hosts and everything in it, the sea and everything in it. You gave life to them all. The hosts of heaven worship you, and the heaven of heavens glorifies you,
because you alone are the Lord our God. You chose Abram and brought him out of the land of the Chaldeans, and you gave him the name Abraham.

And you found his heart faithful before you, and you made a covenant with him to give him the land of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Jebusites, and Girgashites, and to his descendants forever. You fulfilled your words, because you are righteous.
And you saw the affliction of our ancestors in Egypt and heard their cry at the Red Sea.

And you performed a sign for them in Egypt, against Pharaoh, all his servants, and all the people of his land, because you knew that they had acted arrogantly against your people. You made a great name for yourself that remains to this day.
And you divided the Red Sea before them, and they passed through the sea as though on dry ground. You drowned their pursuers like stones in deep waters.
And you led them by a pillar of cloud during the day and by a pillar of fire at night, to light the paths along which they traveled.
And you came down upon Mount Sinai and spoke with them from heaven. You gave them just judgments, true laws, and good decrees and commandments.
And you made your holy Sabbaths known to them, and you gave them commandments, decrees, and laws through Moses your servant.

And you gave them bread from heaven for food, and you made water flow from the rock and gave them drink. You opened the way for them to enter and take possession of the land that you had raised your hand to give them.
But our fathers themselves became arrogant and acted lawlessly. They stiffened their necks and did not listen to your commandments.

And they disregarded your laws and did not remember the wonders you had performed among them. Instead, they stiffened their necks, turned their backs, and wanted to return to slavery in Egypt. But you, Lord our God, are compassionate and merciful, patient and abounding in mercy, and you did not reject them completely.
And again they made themselves a cast calf and said, “These are the gods who brought us up from the land of the Egyptians,” and they committed great provocations.

And in your great compassion and mercy, you did not abandon them or scatter them in the wilderness. You did not take away from them the pillar of cloud that led them during the day, or the pillar of fire that gave them light at night on the paths they traveled.
And you gave them your good Holy Spirit to understand the laws. You did not withhold the manna from their mouths, and you gave them water from the rock for their thirst.
And you led them about in the wilderness for forty years. Their clothes did not wear out, and their shoes did not grow old.
And you struck down kings and peoples before them, and they divided their land and took possession of it as an inheritance: the land of Sihon, king of Heshbon, and the land of Og, king of Bashan.
And you multiplied their children like the stars of heaven, and you brought them into the land you had promised to their fathers, and they took possession of it.

For you destroyed the inhabitants of the land, the Canaanites, before them, and you gave their land into their hands. You destroyed their kings and the people of the land just as they wished, according to their desires.

And they captured towering cities and walls, and took possession of houses filled with every good thing, wells dug and prepared, vineyards, olive trees, and every kind of fruit-bearing tree, providing abundant food for them. They ate and were satisfied, grew fat, and lived in luxury amid the great good things you gave them.
And they went away and became estranged from you, and turned back from your laws. They killed your prophets, who preached to them to return to you, and they greatly provoked you to anger.

And you gave them into the hands of their oppressors, who oppressed them. They cried out to you in the times of their distress, and you heard them from heaven. In your great compassion and mercy, you saved them and brought them out of the hands of their oppressors.

And when they were at rest, they turned back and did evil in your sight. You left them in the hands of their enemies, who tormented them. Again they cried out to you, and you heard them from heaven and delivered them in your great mercy.

And again you warned them to return to your laws, but they, made senseless by foolishness, did not listen to your laws. They sinned against your commands and your commandments, which you had spoken and commanded, saying that whoever among mankind carries out the words of your commandments will live by them. But they turned their backs, became stiff-necked, and did not listen to your word.

And you were patient with them and sent the prophets to warn them through your Holy Spirit. Yet even then they did not listen, and you handed them over to the foreign peoples of the land, who afflicted them greatly.

And according to your great compassion and mercy, you did not abandon them completely, nor did you reject them and banish them from you, for you are mighty, compassionate and merciful, patient and abundant in mercy.

And now, Lord our God, powerful and great, almighty and awesome, righteous and true, keep your covenant and mercy, and look upon the suffering and distress of us, our kings, our rulers, our priests, our prophets, all our ancestors, and your people, whom the kings of Assyria have afflicted, oppressing us to this day.
And you are righteous in everything you have brought upon us because of our sins, for you have acted faithfully.
For we have sinned, together with our kings, our rulers, our priests, and our ancestors. We have not carried out your commandments or paid attention to your laws and the warnings you gave us.

Despite your compassion and the many good things you gave us, and in this wide, spacious, fertile land that you gave us, we did not know how to serve you. Instead, we turned our hearts away from your laws, and we were handed over into captivity because of our sins.
And behold, today we are in slavery, as is this land that you gave our ancestors so that they could freely eat its fruit and its good things.

Now, today, foreign kings rule over us and consume its produce because of our sins. Having fallen into slavery, we pay tribute, and they control us and our livestock as they wish. Today we are in great distress and sorrow because of our sins.

And now, because of all this, we make a covenant and pledge our faithfulness. We believe in your laws and carry them out, along with everything written in them. We confirm these words in writing, and all our rulers, our Levites, and our priests seal them.
And these are those who seal this document of faithfulness to you: Nehemiah son of Hacaliah, and Zedekiah son of Seraiah,
and Azariah and Jeremiah,
and Pashhur, Amariah, Malchijah,
Hattush, Shebaniah, Malluch,
Harim, Meremoth, Obadiah,
Daniel, Ginnethon, Baruch,
Meshullam, Abijah, Mijamin,
Maaziah, Bilgai, Shimei. All these are priests.
And the Levites: Jeshua son of Azaniah, Binnui of the sons of Henadad, Kadmiel,
and their brothers: Shebaniah, Hodiah, Kelita, Pelaiah, Hanan,
Mica, Rehob, Sebi,
Zaccur, Sherebiah, Shebaniah,
Hodiah, the sons of Banuniah.
The leaders of the people: Parosh, Pahath-moab, Elam, Zattu.
The sons of Bani, Azgad, and Bebai.
Adonijah, Bigvai, Adin, Ater.
Hezekiah, Azzur, Hodiah, Hashum, Bezai.
Hariph, Anathoth, Nebai.
Magpiash, Meshullam, Hezir.
Meshezabel, Zadok, Jaddua.
Pelatiah, Hanan, Anaiah.
Hoshea, Hananiah.
Rehum, Hashabnah, Maaseiah.
Ahiah, Hanan, Anan.
Malluch, Rehum.

And the rest of the people—the priests, the Levites, the gatekeepers, the singers, the temple servants, and all of us, the people who hear the law of the Lord our God—bear witness today before you: men and women, their sons and daughters.

We confirm by an oath today before you that whoever transgresses your laws shall be under a curse and condemnation, whoever does not keep your law, which was given through Moses your servant. Rather, with all our willingness, we shall keep and carry out all the commandments of the Lord God, his judgments, and his decrees.
We shall not give our daughters to the sons of foreign peoples, nor shall we take the daughters of the nations as wives for our sons.
If the peoples of this land bring merchandise to us on the Sabbath day, we shall not buy from them on the Sabbath, because it is a holy day, and we shall keep the seventh day holy.
We shall give as contributions a third of a didrachma each year for the building of the house of God.

And for the bread of the Presence, the sacrifices at their appointed times, the burnt offerings at all the festivals, the yearly observances, the Sabbaths, the new moons, the dedications, the holy offerings, and the sin offerings that make atonement for Israel, and for the work of the temple of the Lord our God.

We shall cast lots for the allotment of wood that falls to the priests and the Levites, and the people shall bring it to the house of our God, according to our ancestral households, at appointed times each year, to be burned on the sacrificial altar of the Lord our God, as it is written in the law of Moses.
We shall give the firstfruits of our land and the fruit of our trees each year to the house of the Lord our God.

We shall bring the two-drachma payments for our firstborn sons and the firstborn of our livestock, as it is written in the law of Moses, and the firstborn of our cattle and flocks to the house of our God, to our priests, the Levites who serve in the house of the Lord.
We shall bring the firstfruits of our wheat, the fruit of our trees, wine, and oil to the priests, to the treasury of God. The Levites shall go around and collect the whole of the tithes of our land.

There shall be a priest, a son of Aaron, who shall collect a tithe from the Levites, and the Levites shall give a tithe of our tithes to the high priest, in the house of our God, in the treasury rooms that are in the temple of the Lord.

For he shall be there to store it in the storerooms of the Levites and the attendants, in the places where the sacred utensils are. It shall be for the priests, the Levites, the gatekeepers, and the singers of psalms. May their provisions never fail from the house of our God, and may they not interrupt the service of the Lord.

The leaders of the people settled in Jerusalem, and they cast lots so that one in ten, whoever was chosen by lot, would settle in Jerusalem, the holy city, and the other nine would go to their respective towns.
The people blessed those men who set themselves apart and settled in Jerusalem.
These are the leaders of the land who settled in Jerusalem, and the priests, the Levites, the Nethinim, and the descendants of Solomon’s servants.

Those who settled in Jerusalem were from the tribes of Judah and Benjamin. These were from the sons of Judah: Athaiah son of Uzziah, son of Zechariah, son of Amariah, son of Shephatiah, son of Mahalalel, from the sons of Perez;
and Maaseiah son of Baruch, son of Ahaz, son of Uzziah, son of Adaiah, son of Joiarib, son of Zechariah, son of Shiloni.
All the descendants of Perez who settled in Jerusalem: four hundred sixty-eight mighty men.
These were the sons of Benjamin: Sallu son of Meshullam, son of Joed, son of Pedaiah, son of Kolaiah, son of Maaseiah, son of Ithiel, son of Isaiah.
After him were Gabbai and Sallai: nine hundred forty-eight.
Joses son of Zichri was their overseer and supervisor, and Judah son of Hassenuah was second in command in the city.
From the priests: Jedaiah son of Joiarib;
Jachin; Seraiah son of Hilkiah, son of Meshullam, son of Zadok, son of Meraioth, son of Ahitub. Their houses were near the temple of the Lord.

Their brothers who performed the work of service in the house of the Lord numbered eight hundred twenty-two. And Adaiah son of Jeroham, son of Pelaliah, son of Amasiah, son of Zechariah, son of Pashhur, son of Malchijah;
And his brothers, heads of ancestral families: two hundred forty-two; and Amashsai son of Azriel.
and their brothers, mighty men, numbered one hundred twenty-eight. Their overseer and supervisor was Zichriel, who was among the great rulers.
From the Levites: Shemaiah son of Hasshub, son of Hezron;
and Mattaniah [?], son of Micah, and Joreb, sons of Shammua: two hundred seventy-four.
The gatekeepers were Akkub, Talmon, and his brothers: one hundred seventy-two.
The overseer and supervisor of the Levites in Jerusalem was Uzzi son of Bani, son of Hashabiah, son of Mattaniah, son of Micah, from the sons of Asaph, who were singers near the house of the Lord.
For the king's command to them was to remain there and maintain the service without interruption.
And Pethahiah son of Meshezabel, Zerah son of Judah, who had charge of all the arrangements on the king's behalf and lived on his estate.
From the sons of Judah, some settled in Kiriath-arba, Jeshua, and Beersheba, and their dwelling place was Lachish,
and their estates; they also possessed Beersheba.
The sons of Benjamin were in Geba,
Michmash; and the Levites' portion was in Judah and Benjamin.
These were the priests and Levites who came up with Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and Jeshua son of Jozadak: Seraiah, Jeremiah, Ezra, Amariah, Malluch, Hattush, and Shecaniah.
These were the leaders of the priests and their brothers in the days of Jeshua.
The Levites were Jeshua, Binnui, Kadmiel, Sherebiah, Judah, Mattaniah, and their brothers, who were assigned duties day by day. Joiakim's son was Eliashib,

Eliashib's son was Joiada, Joiada's son was Jonathan, and Jonathan's son was Jaddua. In the days of Joiakim, his brothers were leaders and priests of the ancestral houses: Seraiah, Meraiah, Jeremiah, Hananiah, Azariah, Ezra, Meshullam, Amariah, Johanan, and Malluch.
The Levites in the days of Eliashib, Joiada, Joah, Johanan, and Jaddua were recorded as heads of ancestral houses. All these were priests during the reign of Darius.
The sons of Levi who were heads of ancestral houses were recorded in the chronicle register down to Johanan son of Eliashib.
And the leaders of the Levites—Hashabiah, Sherebiah, Jeshua, the sons of Kadmiel, and his brothers beside him—were to praise and sing psalms, as David the man of God had commanded,
day after day, continually, in their assemblies, together with the gatekeepers.
These served in the days of Joiakim son of Jeshua, son of Jehozadak, and in the days of Nehemiah and Ezra, the priest and scribe of the law of the Lord.

At the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem, they sought out the Levites in their own places to bring them to Jerusalem and celebrate the dedication with joy, thanksgiving, and songs, with musical instruments, cymbals, drums, and harps, and with the sound of a horn trumpet.
All those who sang songs and psalms gathered from every region around Jerusalem.
From their towns, villages, and settlements, to come to Jerusalem for the service of worship.
All the priests and Levites purified themselves, and they purified the people and the gatekeepers of the great gates of the wall.
They brought the leaders of Judah up onto the wall, and they went behind them with songs and musical instruments, two by two:
Hoshaiah, Uzziah, and half the leaders of Judah,
Azariah, Ezra, and Meshullam,
Judah, Benjamin, Shemaiah, and Jeremiah.
Among the sons of the priests were those who sounded the trumpets: Zechariah son of Jonathan, son of Shemaiah, son of Mattaniah, son of Micaiah, son of Zaccur, son of Asaph.

And their brothers, Shemaiah and Azriel, blessed the songs and psalms of David, the man of God, which he played. And Ezra the scribe walked before them over the gates, and those who sang walked opposite him.
They went up the steps of the City of David, at the ascent of the wall above David’s palaces, as far as the Water Gate of Ephraim and along the eastern side,
and to the Gate of [?], to the Tower of Hananel, and as far as the Fountain Gate. The sound of the songs could be heard everywhere, for Ezra had commanded them to stand over all the gates and sing.

On that day they offered great sacrifices and rejoiced greatly, because God had made them rejoice with great joy. Their wives and children also rejoiced, and the sound of their joy could be heard from Jerusalem as far as distant places.

On that day they appointed men over the treasury of the treasures, the firstfruits, the tithes, and everything gathered there from the city’s leaders for the priests and Levites, as commanded in the law of Moses. For there was great joy in Judah and among the priests and Levites. Those who were singers, psalm-singers, and gatekeepers took care of God’s holy things and maintained holiness, as David and his son Solomon had prescribed.
For in the days of David, Asaph was the chief and leader of the songs of the psalms; they played, sang, and glorified God.

All Israel, in the days of Zerubbabel and in the days of Nehemiah, gave the allotted portions to the singers and gatekeepers, day by day, as prescribed. They sanctified the Levites, and the Levites sanctified the sons of Aaron.
On that day they read the book of Moses in the hearing of the people, and this was found written in it: “No Ammonite or Moabite shall ever enter the assembly of God,
because they did not come out to meet the Israelites with bread and water, but hired Balaam the diviner to curse them. Yet our God turned the curses into a blessing.”
When they heard the law, they separated all the mixed population from Israel.
Before this, Eliashib was priest in charge of the treasury of the house of our God, and he gave Tobiah a place

and built himself a large storeroom there. This was formerly the place where they deposited the manna, the frankincense, the sacred utensils, the tithes of grain, wine, olive oil, and oil—the provisions for the Levites, singers, and gatekeepers—and the firstfruits for the priests.
While all this was being done, I was not in Jerusalem, for in the thirty-second year of Artaxerxes king of the Babylonians I went to the king, and after many days I asked the king for leave.
And I went up to Jerusalem and learned of all the evil that Eliashib had done for Tobiah, for he had allowed him to build a storeroom in the courtyard of the house of the Lord.
This seemed very wrong to me, and I threw all Tobiah’s belongings out of the storeroom.
And I ordered the Lord’s storeroom to be purified, and I brought back there the furnishings and utensils of the house of the Lord, the manna, and the frankincense.
And I learned and discovered that the Levites’ portions had not been given to them. They had gone to their own fields, and the Levites and singers were doing farm work.
And I confronted the officials and said, “Why have provisions ceased in the house of the Lord?” And I gathered all the attendants and appointed them to their places.
And all the Jews brought the tithes of grain, wine, and oil into the storehouse of the house of the Lord.

And I ordered that these be entrusted to Shelemiah the priest, Zadok the scribe, and Pedaiah, who was one of the Levites, and under their authority to Hanan son of Zaccur, son of Mattaniah, because those who distributed and gave portions to their brothers were trustworthy.
May God remember me in all this and not take his mercy away from me, because I did all this in the house of the Lord, the God of Israel.

In those days I saw in Judea that people were treading winepresses on the Sabbath and bringing produce through the gates of Jerusalem. They loaded pack animals with wine, grapes, and figs, and brought loads into Jerusalem on the Sabbath. And I called witnesses because they were selling on the Sabbath.
And those who brought fish and all kinds of merchandise sat in the marketplaces, and the Jews bought from them on the Sabbath inside Jerusalem.
And I confronted the Jews who were in Jerusalem and the officials of Judah, and said to them, “What is this lawlessness that you are committing, profaning the holy Sabbath days?
Did not your fathers act this way, so that God brought all these calamities upon them and upon this city? And now why are you increasing the wrath against Israel and profaning the holy Sabbath day?”

And when I set up the gates of Jerusalem before the Sabbath, I ordered the gates to be shut and did not allow them to be opened until the Sabbath had passed. And I also stationed young men as guards so that no one would dare enter through the gates of Jerusalem with a load on the Sabbath.
And all those who sold goods spent the night outside Jerusalem once or twice.
And I said to them, “Why do you spend the night outside this wall? If I see this lawlessness of yours again, I will issue this order: you are not to enter on our Sabbaths or come into this city.”

And I spoke to the Levites, who had been purified and came and guarded the gates and performed purification on the Sabbath day. From then on they did not profane the Sabbaths. And for all this may God remember me and spare me according to his abundant mercy.
And in those days I saw that the Jews had married women from Ashdod, Ammon, and Moab.
And their sons and some of the women spoke the language of Ashdod and did not know how to speak Hebrew.

And I confronted them and cursed them, and I struck many of their men. And I made them swear in the name of God not to give their daughters to those people’s sons and not to take those people’s daughters for their own sons.

And I said to them, “Did not Solomon king of Israel sin in all this? And who among all our kings was as wise as he? He was beloved by God, and God appointed him king over all Israel. Yet foreign women led even such a man, beloved by God, wise, and a great king, astray and caused him to fall into sin.
And now, let me not hear that anyone commits such great evils, sins against God, and takes a foreign woman as his wife.”
And I heard from the sons of Joiada and from Eliashib the high priest that his wife was a daughter of Sanballat, and I rejected him and drove him away from me.
May God remember them in the inheritance and in the covenant of the priesthood.
And I purified the Levites from all foreigners, and I arranged and organized them day by day—the priests and the Levites, each man for his own work.

And I made arrangements to bring all the wood for the burnt offerings at each appointed time, and the firstfruits of their produce. May our God remember me for all my good deeds of righteousness, he who is blessed forever. Amen.
